67:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Mulk Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj bin Muhammad and Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abbas al-Jashmi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is a surah in the Qur’an with thirty verses that will intercede for its reciter until he is forgiven: Tabarak al-Ladi bi-Yadihil-Mulk.” The four scholars of Sunan narrated it on the authority of Shu`bah, and al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith. Al-Hafiz Ibn `Asakir narrated in his history in the biography of Ahmad bin Nasr bin Ziyad Abu `Abdullah al-Qurashi al-Naysaburi al-Muqri, the ascetic jurist, one of the trustworthy narrators from whom al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, but not in the two Sahihs. Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated from him, and he studied jurisprudence according to the school of Abu `Ubayd bin Harbuyeh and many others. He cited with his chain of transmission from his hadith on the authority of Furat bin al-Sa`ib, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from among those who came before you died and he had nothing with him from the Book of God except Tabarak. When he was placed in his grave, the angel came to him.” Then the sura rose up in his face, so he said to her, You are from the Book of God, and I hate to offend you, and I do not possess any harm or benefit for you, for him, or for myself. If you want this from him, then go to the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, and intercede for him. So she goes to the Lord and says, O Lord, so-and-so has come to me from among Your Book, so teach me and recite to me. Will You burn him with fire and torment him while I am in his stomach? If you are going to do that to him, then erase me from your book. He will say, Do I not see that you are angry? You will say, And it is right for me to be angry. He will say, Go, for I have given him to you and made you my intercessor for him. He said, So you come and rebuke the angel, and he will go out, downcast, having done nothing to him. He said, “So you come and put your mouth over his mouth and say, ‘Welcome to this mouth, for perhaps it will recite it to me. Welcome to this chest, for perhaps it will suffer. Welcome to these two feet, for perhaps they will stand with me, and it will keep him company in his grave, fearing loneliness for him.” He said, “So when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told this, there remained neither young nor old, free nor slave, but that he learned it, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called it Al-Munjiyyah.” I said: This is a very strange hadith. Furat bin Al-Sa’ib was declared weak by Imam Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’in, Al-Bukhari, Abu Hatim, Al-Daraqutni, and more than one person. Ibn Asakir mentioned it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Zuhri, in an abbreviated version. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the book Ithbat Adhab Al-Gabar on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with both chains of transmission ending with him and at the beginning of the chain of transmission ending with him, that which supports this. We wrote it in the book Al-Jana’iz of Al-Ahkam Al-Kubra, and praise and thanks be to God. Al-Tabarani and Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi narrated on the authority of Salam bin Maskeen on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A surah in the Qur’an argued on behalf of its reciter until it brought him into Paradise: Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion.” Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, Yahya ibn Malik al-Nakri narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “One of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, pitched his tent over a grave, not realizing that it was a grave. There was a man reciting Surat al-Mulk until he completed it. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I pitched my tent over a grave, not realizing that it was a grave, and there was a man reciting Surat al-Mulk, Tabarak, until he completed it.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is the protector, it is the savior, it saves him from the punishment of the grave.’ Then he said: This is a strange hadith from this chain of transmission, and in this chapter there is a hadith from Abu Hurayrah. Then al-Tirmidhi also narrated on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited ‘Alif, Lam, Meem’ The Revelation and ‘Tabarak al-ladhi bi yadihi al-mulk’. Layth said on the authority of Tawus: ‘They are superior to every surah in the Qur’an by seventy good deeds.’” Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ajlan al-Asbahani narrated to us, Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Abaan narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I would that it were in the heart of every person of my nation, meaning Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion. This hadith is strange, and Ibrahim is weak. A similar narration has been presented before in Surat Yasin. Abd ibn Humayd narrated this hadith in a more detailed manner than this, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said to a man: Shall I not give you a treat that will make you happy? He said: Yes. He said: “Recite ‘Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion’ and teach it to your family, all your children, the children of your house, and your neighbors, for it is the savior and debater. It will debate or dispute with its reader on the Day of Resurrection before its Lord, and will ask Him to save him from the torment of the Fire and save its reciter from the torment of the grave.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I would that it were in the heart of every person of my nation. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty glorifies His noble self and informs us that in His hand is dominion, meaning He is the One who disposes of all creation as He wills. There is no questioning of His judgment, nor is He questioned about what He does due to His power, wisdom, and justice. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And He has power over all things. Then He the Almighty said: Who created death and life. This verse was used as evidence by those who said that death is an existential matter, because it is created. The meaning of the verse is that He created creation from nothingness to test them, that is, to examine them as to which of them is best in deeds, as God the Almighty said: How do you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? So He called the first state, which is nothingness, death and called this creation life. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then He causes you to die, then He brings you to life. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding God the Almighty’s statement: Who created death and life, he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say: God humiliated the children of Adam with death and made this world a home of life, then a home of death, and He made the Hereafter a home of reward, then a home of eternity. Muammar narrated it on the authority of Qatadah. And the Almighty’s saying: That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed means best in deed as Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan said, and He did not say most in deed. Then the Almighty said: And He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving meaning He is the Exalted in Might, the Great, the Invincible, and He is, in addition to that, Forgiving to whoever repents to Him and returns to Him after having disobeyed Him and gone against His command. And if the Almighty is Exalted in Might, He, in addition to that, forgives, has mercy, pardons, and overlooks. Then the Almighty said: Who created seven heavens in layers meaning layer after layer. Are they connected in the sense that they are above one another or are they separated by spaces between them? There are two opinions, the second of which is more correct, as indicated by the hadith of the Night Journey and others. And the Almighty said: You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any inconsistency meaning, rather, it is consistent and level, with no difference, discord, contradiction, deficiency, defect, or flaw in it. For this reason, the Almighty said: Then return your sight; do you see any fault? meaning, look at the sky and contemplate it; do you see in it any fault, deficiency, defect, or flaw. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ath-Thawri, and others said regarding the Almighty’s statement: Then return your sight; do you see any fault? meaning, cracks. As-Suddi said, Do you see any fault? meaning, holes. Ibn Abbas said in another narration, Of faults, meaning, of holes. Qatadah said, Do you see any fault? meaning, do you see any flaw, O son of Adam? And the Almighty’s saying: Then return your sight twice. Qatada said: twice. Your sight will return to you humbled. Ibn Abbas said: humiliated. Mujahid and Qatada said: humbled. And it is weary. Ibn Abbas said: meaning while it is exhausted. Mujahid, Qatada and As-Suddi said: Weary is the one who is cut off from exhaustion. The meaning of the verse is that if you were to repeat your sight as many times as you repeat it, we would not return to you, meaning your sight would return to you humiliated, unable to see a fault or defect. And it is weary, meaning tired, cut off from exhaustion from repeated repetition, and it will not see any deficiency. And when He denied any deficiency in its creation, He explained its perfection and its adornment by saying: And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, which are the planets that were placed in it, of the moving and fixed stars. God the Almighty says: {And We have made them missiles for the devils} The pronoun in His statement {And We have made them} refers to the type of lamps, not to them themselves, because He does not throw stars in the sky, but meteors below them, and they may be derived from them, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: {And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze} meaning, We have made this humiliation for the devils in this world and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze in the Hereafter, as God the Almighty says at the beginning of Surat al-Saffat 37:{Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars, * And as protection from every rebellious devil. * They do not hear the assembly on high, and they are pelted from every side, * Driven away, and for them is a lasting punishment, * Except for him who snatches a snatch; then a piercing flame pursues him.} Qatadah said: God created these stars for three reasons: they were created as adornments for the heaven, as missiles for the devils, and as signs by which people are guided. Whoever interprets them otherwise has spoken according to his own opinion, wasted his share, and assumed what he has no knowledge of. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

67:12: God the Almighty says, informing about the one who fears the position of his Lord in private when he is absent from people, and refrains from sins and performs acts of obedience where no one can see him except God the Almighty, that he will have forgiveness and a great reward, meaning his sins will be forgiven and he will be rewarded with a great reward, as proven in the two Sahihs: “Seven whom God the Almighty will shade in the shade of His Throne on the Day when there will be no shade except His shade. Then he said, pointing out that He is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts: “Whether you conceal your speech or declare it publicly. Indeed, He is All-Knowing of that within the breasts,” meaning what goes through the hearts. Does He who created not know? That is, does the Creator not know? It was also said that it means, Does God not know His creation? The first is more appropriate, because He said: And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware. Then He mentioned His blessing upon His creation in subjecting the earth to them and making it subservient to them by making it a calm continent that does not shake or tremble, by what He placed in it of mountains and made springs gush forth in it, and made paths in it, and prepared in it benefits and places for crops and fruits, so the Most High said: It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its paths. That is, travel wherever you wish in its regions and go around its regions and corners in various types of earnings and trade, and know that your striving will not benefit you at all unless God makes it easy for you. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Ibn Hibban. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. So He confirmed for her a coming and going in order to seek provision while putting her trust in God, the Almighty, for He is the One who is subjected, the One who is caused. And to Him is the resurrection meaning the return on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Suddi and Qatadah said: Its paths are its edges, its valleys and its regions. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah also said: Its paths are the mountains. 67:28: God the Almighty says: Say O Muhammad to these polytheists who deny His blessings, "Have you considered: if God should destroy me and those with me or have mercy on us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?" That is, free yourselves, for there is no one who can save you from God except repentance, turning to Him, and returning to His religion. The torment and punishment you wish for us will not benefit you, for whether God punishes us or has mercy on us, you have no escape from His torment and painful punishment that will befall you. Then God the Almighty says: Say, 'He is the Most Gracious, we have believed in Him, and upon Him we rely.' That is, we believe in the Lord of the Worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and upon Him we rely in all our affairs, as God the Almighty says: So worship Him and put your trust in Him. For this reason God the Almighty says: Then you will know who is in manifest error, that is, who is from us and who will have the final outcome in this world and the hereafter. Then God the Almighty said, showing His mercy to His creation: Say, ‘Have you considered if your water were to become sunken?’ That is, if it were to sink into the earth and could not be reached by blacksmith’s axes or strong arms? Sunken is the opposite of springing. That is why God the Almighty said: Then who can bring you flowing water? That is, a flowing spring that runs on the surface of the earth. That is, no one is able to do that except God the Almighty. So it is from His grace and generosity that He made water spring forth for you and made it flow in all parts of the earth according to what the servants need of it, whether little or much. So to God be praise and thanks. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Mulk. To God be praise and thanks.
